topStories.headline: Fieldwork Brewing Signs Lease at Presidio, Set to Become Park's First Taproom
topStories.dek: Berkeley's acclaimed craft brewery will take over the long-dark former Presidio Social Club space at 563 Ruger Street, with an early 2027 opening targeted.
topStories.body:
The Presidio Trust has signed a lease with Fieldwork Brewing Company for the full commercial restaurant property at 563 Ruger Street in the Presidio, near the Lombard Gate and the Letterman campus. The Berkeley-born brewery — known for award-winning small-batch craft beers and community-oriented taprooms — will become the Presidio's first dedicated brewery taproom, joining a growing roster of food and beverage destinations inside the national park site.

The historic property features approximately 5,370 square feet of flexible indoor space, 1,780 square feet of outdoor deck space, and on-site parking. Fieldwork's Presidio location will feature an expansive beverage program including craft beer, cocktails, and non-alcoholic options, alongside a full-service food menu and a specialty brunch offering — in a first for the brewery, a full cocktail program will also be introduced. The project will mark Fieldwork's third San Francisco location, joining its existing presence at China Basin Park and Mission Rock.

The space at 563 Ruger has been largely without a dining draw since the Presidio Social Club shut its doors in May 2024 after an 18-year run. Fieldwork plans to renovate the kitchen and add private event space, giving the historic former military barracks interior a needed refresh. The taproom is projected to open in early 2027.

"Fieldwork at the Presidio will be a touchstone for our company for years to come," said Barry Braden, co-founder and CEO of Fieldwork Brewing Company, in the official press release. "We look for locations that create a true destination experience for our guests, and the Presidio offers just that."

topStories.headline: Outside Lands Music Festival Returns to Golden Gate Park This Weekend
topStories.dek: The annual three-day festival, headlined by Charli XCX, The Strokes, and RÜFÜS DU SOL, runs August 7–9 and will draw tens of thousands of visitors to the southern edge of the Richmond.
topStories.body:
Outside Lands Music Festival returns to Golden Gate Park for three days of music, food, wine, art, and more, running August 7–9, 2026. The festival — celebrating its 19th year — features headliners Charli XCX on Friday, The Strokes on Saturday, and RÜFÜS DU SOL closing out Sunday, alongside a wide range of supporting acts across multiple stages including Turnstile, Modest Mouse, The xx, PinkPantheress, Baby Keem, Death Cab for Cutie, and many more.

Festival gates open at 11 a.m. each day, with music starting at noon. Richmond District residents with neighborhood parking permits should note that street parking will be extremely limited throughout the weekend, with an estimated 75,000 daily attendees. Mission Local's Richmond Buzz column notes that while the festival can create headaches for local drivers, the influx of visitors is often a boost for neighborhood businesses along Clement Street and Geary Boulevard.

Both three-day and single-day passes are sold out through official channels, though resale tickets remain available. The festival takes place at Golden Gate Park, just south of the Outer Richmond. Residents near the park are encouraged to review the festival's neighbor letter on the Outside Lands website for information on planned road closures and parking impacts.

topStories.headline: Geary Boulevard Infrastructure Overhaul Enters New Phase as SFMTA Improvements Loom
topStories.dek: The SFPUC's $50 million underground water and sewer project along Geary Boulevard is on track, with SFMTA set to begin above-ground safety and transit upgrades in late 2026.
topStories.body:
The San Francisco Public Utilities Commission's major infrastructure project along the two-mile Geary Boulevard corridor in the Richmond District — spanning from 32nd Avenue to Stanyan Street — continues to progress, with crews having completed replacement of the sewer main in Segment A (32nd Avenue to 12th Avenue) and advancing work on water distribution and transmission lines.

The $50 million project, which began in January 2025, is replacing or rehabilitating approximately 1.4 miles of sewer mains and 6.7 miles of water pipes, most of which are over 120 years old and date back to the late 1800s. The SFPUC notes that Geary Boulevard remains open during construction, with two lanes available in both directions in most active work zones, and that driveway access for residents and businesses is being maintained.

Looking ahead, the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency is set to join the project in late 2026 to add above-ground pedestrian safety and bus improvements along the corridor, including bus and pedestrian curb extensions (bulb-outs), upgraded traffic signals, full roadway paving, and neighborhood enhancements such as new trees and decorative sidewalks at selected bus stops. The SFPUC urges residents to support Geary Boulevard small businesses during the construction period.

events.title: EXCLUSION: The Presidio's Role in WWII Japanese American Incarceration
events.location: Presidio Officers' Club, 50 Moraga Avenue, Presidio
events.description: The Presidio Trust's award-winning free exhibition examines the Presidio's role in the unjust incarceration of 120,000 Japanese Americans during World War II. Open Fridays–Sundays, 10 a.m.–4 p.m., through August 31.

events.title: I Am An American: The Nisei Soldier Experience
events.location: Military Intelligence Service Historic Learning Center, 640 Mason Street, Presidio
events.description: A 1,500-square-foot national traveling exhibition recounting the history of Japanese American soldiers who served during World War II. Open Fridays–Tuesdays, noon–5 p.m., through August 31; free for veterans, children 12 and under, and NJAHS members; $15 for all others.

events.title: SFPL SummerMobile at Presidio Tunnel Tops
events.location: Presidio Tunnel Tops, 210 Lincoln Blvd, Presidio
events.description: The San Francisco Public Library's SummerMobile makes weekly Wednesday stops at Presidio Tunnel Tops from 10 a.m. to noon through August 13, offering book browsing, checkouts, and SFPL resources for all ages.

events.title: Outside Lands Music Festival 2026
events.location: Golden Gate Park (Marx Meadow entrance at 25th Ave & Fulton), Outer Richmond border
events.description: The 19th annual Outside Lands festival runs August 7–9 in Golden Gate Park, headlined by Charli XCX, The Strokes, and RÜFÜS DU SOL across multiple stages. Gates open at 11 a.m. daily; passes are sold out through official channels.

events.title: SFPL SummerMobile at Presidio Tunnel Tops — Final Stop
events.location: Presidio Tunnel Tops, 210 Lincoln Blvd, Presidio
events.description: The last Wednesday SummerMobile stop at Presidio Tunnel Tops for the 2026 season, running 10 a.m.–noon. Browse, check out materials, and pick up a Bookmobile Explorer Map sticker; no registration required.

events.title: Heart of the Richmond District Night Market — Final Summer Event
events.location: Clement Street between 22nd and 25th Avenues, Outer Richmond
events.description: The final Heart of the Richmond District Night Market of the summer season runs 4–8 p.m., featuring food and clothing vendors, live performances on two stages, DJs, family-friendly activities, and a pet show. Free and open to the public.
events.sourceName: Heart of the Richmond District Night Market

events.title: 250 Years on the Presidio — Monthly Ranger Walk
events.location: Presidio Visitor Center, 210 Lincoln Blvd (near Anza), Presidio
events.description: Walk the Tunnel Tops and historic Main Post of the Presidio with an expert NPS guide, exploring the many layers of nature and history from the Ohlone people to the present day, as part of the Presidio's 250th anniversary commemorations.

events.title: Presidio Habitat Stewards Volunteer Day
events.description: Volunteer to help restore unique San Francisco coastal habitat at Presidio Tunnel Tops, running 9 a.m.–noon. Part of an ongoing monthly series with the Golden Gate National Parks Conservancy.

moreNews.headline: Clement Street HI NRG Pop-Up Closes Sunday Before Moving to Permanent Geary Home
moreNews.body: The Clement Street HI NRG pop-up — which has operated out of 443 Clement St. near 6th Avenue, the former site of wine bar High Treason — is holding its last day celebration this Sunday, August 9, before relocating to a permanent spot on Geary Boulevard. The send-off event features DJs and free drip coffee. The move signals another shift in the ever-evolving Clement Street retail landscape, according to Mission Local's Richmond Buzz column published this week.

moreNews.headline: Green Apple Books Turns 59, Remains a Clement Street Cornerstone
moreNews.body: Green Apple Books on Clement Street, a Richmond District institution since 1967, continues to anchor the neighborhood's literary life in its 59th year. The two-story store is known for its expansive rare book collection, eclectic themed rooms, and handwritten staff reviews. In 2026, the store's Sunset District sister location (Green Apple Books on the Park) opened its upstairs mezzanine to a coworking and social space for writers, per a recent Richmond Review/Sunset Beacon feature. The original Clement Street store at 506 Clement St. remains open daily.

moreNews.headline: Presidio Marks 250th Anniversary With Summer-Long Programs
moreNews.body: The Presidio of San Francisco is marking a major milestone in 2026: the 250th anniversary of the founding of El Presidio de San Francisco on September 17, 1776. The park has anchored its summer season around the commemoration, offering free exhibitions, monthly ranger-led walks, living history programs, and community gatherings throughout the summer. Key exhibitions — including EXCLUSION at the Officers' Club and I Am An American at the Military Intelligence Service Historic Learning Center — both run through August 31 and are free or low-cost. The Presidio's GO Shuttle fleet also added four new electric, low-floor buses this spring, making the park more accessible.

moreNews.headline: Bi-Rite Market Rumored for Sea Cliff/Lake Street Corridor
moreNews.body: Speculation is growing in the Richmond that Bi-Rite Market — the beloved San Francisco grocer that started on 18th Street — may be eyeing a location at 6001 California St., a space that has been vacant since 2024. Mission Local's Richmond Buzz reported in March 2026 that signs in the window appeared to signal a new tenant, and Bi-Rite CEO Patrick Mills confirmed the company is looking to expand into the neighborhood, though declined to confirm the specific California Street address. City filings show no business has been registered at that location since 2024, and Mills noted there is "still a ways to go" before any outpost opens in the area.

restaurants.name: Burma Superstar
restaurants.description: The original 1992 Clement Street location that put Burmese cuisine on the SF map, famous for its tea leaf salad, curries, and perennially packed dining room.

restaurants.name: Chapeau
restaurants.description: A beloved Inner Richmond French bistro celebrating 30 years, known for consistent classic cuisine and warm hospitality with à la carte and prix-fixe options.

restaurants.name: Kitchen Istanbul
restaurants.description: An elevated neighborhood Turkish restaurant on Clement Street named one of the Bay Area's Top 100 by the SF Chronicle, featuring mezes, kebabs, and a thoughtful wine program.

restaurants.name: Arsicault Bakery
restaurants.description: The Inner Richmond mothership of SF's most celebrated croissant, named best new bakery in the US by Bon Appétit Magazine, with reliably long weekend lines.

restaurants.name: Wako
restaurants.description: Michelin-starred intimate omakase restaurant on Clement Street offering a seasonal, chef-driven Japanese tasting menu — reservations essential.

restaurants.name: Green Apple Books
restaurants.description: While primarily a legendary bookstore, Green Apple's Clement Street flagship has been a neighborhood gathering spot since 1967 and hosts regular literary events.

restaurants.name: The Plough and Stars
restaurants.description: A classic Irish neighborhood bar on Clement Street with live Celtic music, pints on tap, and a warm, welcoming atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Richmond Republic Draught House
restaurants.description: A neighborhood beer bar with 20-plus rotating taps and seriously good bar food, popular with Richmond regulars.

restaurants.name: High Treason
restaurants.description: A modern neighborhood wine bar on Clement Street with an extensive selection of pours and bar bites, perfect for a casual date or catch-up.

restaurants.name: Breck's
restaurants.description: A stylish wine bar and retail market at the start of Clement Street, also serving coffee, tea, and light bites.

restaurants.name: Cinderella Russian Bakery
restaurants.description: A Richmond institution since 1953 serving piroshki, pirogi, borscht, and classic Russian pastries on Balboa Street.

restaurants.name: Pizzetta 211
restaurants.description: A tiny, beloved Outer Richmond spot with a constantly rotating menu of seasonal thin-crust pizzas — expect a wait and an experience akin to a dinner party.

restaurants.name: Lokma
restaurants.description: A popular Outer Richmond Turkish breakfast and brunch spot known for yogurt pancakes, beautifully spiced eggs, and a legendary Turkish breakfast spread.

restaurants.name: Spices
restaurants.description: A Richmond neighborhood staple for authentic Sichuan cuisine, praised by The Infatuation for its great and generously sized entrees.

restaurants.name: Violet's
restaurants.description: The Outer Richmond sister restaurant to Fiorella, serving elevated American plates like seafood platters, clam toast, and shrimp louie rolls alongside creative cocktails.

restaurants.name: Toy Boat by Jane
restaurants.description: A colorful, kid-friendly Clement Street spot formerly known as Toy Boat Dessert Cafe, now serving ice cream, wraps, and sweet treats.

restaurants.name: Heritage Restaurant & Bar
restaurants.description: Seasonal California cuisine and cocktails served inside a beautifully restored 1908 historic building on Clement Street.

restaurants.name: Mamahuhu
restaurants.description: A fun, fast-casual Chinese-American spot from Michelin-starred chef Brandon Jew (Mister Jiu's), serving mapo tofu, sweet and sour chicken, and other classics.

restaurants.name: Cantina Los Mayas
restaurants.description: San Francisco's first Mexican wine bar, serving Yucatecan-Mexican cuisine alongside an exclusively Mexican wine list on Balboa Street.

restaurants.name: The Bitter End
restaurants.description: A fun neighborhood pub with darts, pool tables, and a menu including shepherd's pie, ideal for unwinding after a long day.

restaurants.name: Dragon Beaux
restaurants.description: An upscale dim sum destination in the Outer Richmond celebrated for photogenic, artfully crafted dumplings and bao.

restaurants.name: Breadbelly
restaurants.description: A beloved Inner Richmond bakery and café known for its kaya toast, macadamia nut croissant tart, and inventive Asian-inspired pastries.

hotels.name: Inn at the Presidio
hotels.description: A National Historic Hotel housed in a restored 1903 Georgian Revival barracks on the Presidio's Main Post, offering 22 spacious rooms, evening wine and cheese receptions, and Golden Gate views.

hotels.name: Lodge at the Presidio
hotels.description: Housed in the landmark Montgomery Street Barracks (built 1895–1897), this Presidio hotel offers complimentary breakfast, outdoor fire pits, and easy access to Tunnel Tops.

hotels.name: Seal Rock Inn
hotels.description: A San Francisco landmark since 1959, this third-generation family-owned inn sits beside Sutro Heights Park and Land's End, offering free parking, ocean views, and an on-site bistro restaurant.

hotels.name: Stanyan Park Hotel
hotels.description: Listed on the National Register of Historic Places, this elegantly restored turn-of-the-century hotel sits across from Golden Gate Park with complimentary wine and cheese hours on weekdays.

hotels.name: Geary Parkway Motel
hotels.description: A recently renovated 20-room motel on Geary Boulevard in the Richmond, offering clean, affordable accommodations near Golden Gate Park and the Richmond District's restaurants.

hotels.name: Travelodge by Wyndham Presidio San Francisco
hotels.description: A conveniently located budget chain motel on Lombard Street, close to the Presidio and offering straightforward accommodations near the Marina border.

shops.name: Green Apple Books
shops.description: A beloved Richmond District cornerstone since 1967, carrying hundreds of thousands of new and used titles across two eclectic floors with handwritten staff reviews throughout.

shops.name: Park Life
shops.type: Hybrid art gallery and design retail store
shops.description: A 1,400-square-foot independent store and gallery co-founded in 2006 on Clement Street, featuring curated art, design books, prints, tees, housewares, and 10 rotating gallery exhibitions per year.

shops.name: Sports Basement Presidio
shops.description: A large, community-oriented sporting goods store inside a historic Presidio building, offering gear for hiking, cycling, skiing, and more alongside regular demo events.

shops.name: Sloat Garden Center
shops.description: A full-service neighborhood garden center serving the Richmond with plants, seeds, soil, and gardening supplies.

shops.name: Aroma Tea Shop
shops.description: A Clement Street specialty shop offering a wide selection of fine loose-leaf teas, teaware, and knowledgeable staff to guide tastings.

shops.name: Tunnel Records
shops.description: A neighborhood record shop attached to the 4-Star Theater on Clement Street, carrying vinyl and supporting local music culture.

shops.name: Western Neighborhoods Project / OpenSFHistory Shop
shops.description: A nonprofit dedicated to preserving western San Francisco neighborhood history, operating a shop at 1617 Balboa Street with local history books, maps, and ephemera.

shops.name: Clement Street Farmers Market
shops.description: A year-round weekly farmers market on Clement Street running Sundays from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m., offering fresh local produce and artisan goods.

shops.name: Foggy Notion
shops.type: Independent home goods and gifts boutique
shops.description: A curated Clement Street boutique specializing in gifts, candles, stationery, and lifestyle goods with a distinctly San Francisco sensibility.

shops.name: Tantrum
shops.description: A fun, eclectic clothing and accessories boutique on Clement Street catering to a range of styles and occasions.

shops.name: Nourish
shops.description: A neighborhood natural foods store in the Inner Richmond carrying supplements, specialty groceries, and wellness products.

artEntertainment.name: Walt Disney Family Museum
artEntertainment.description: A 40,000-square-foot non-profit museum in a restored Presidio barracks dedicated to the life and legacy of Walt Disney, featuring ten permanent interactive galleries and rotating special exhibitions; open Thu–Mon in summer.

artEntertainment.name: Park Life Gallery
artEntertainment.description: The gallery component of Park Life's Clement Street space, curating 10 exhibitions per year of emerging and established contemporary artists and collaborating on limited-edition artist products.

artEntertainment.name: 4-Star Theater
artEntertainment.description: A Richmond District cinema landmark since 1913, now screening independent and international films alongside concerts and events, with a Tunnel Records shop attached.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Tunnel Tops
artEntertainment.type: National park event and recreation space
artEntertainment.description: A 14-acre national park destination atop the Presidio's highway tunnels, hosting free summer festivals, ranger programs, campfire circles, food trucks, and breathtaking Golden Gate Bridge views.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Officers' Club
artEntertainment.type: Historic cultural center and exhibition space
artEntertainment.description: The oldest building in San Francisco, now a free cultural center and event space on the Presidio's Main Post, currently hosting the EXCLUSION exhibition through August 31.

artEntertainment.name: Legion of Honor
artEntertainment.description: A world-class fine arts museum in a neoclassical building overlooking the Golden Gate, housing a permanent collection spanning 4,000 years and presenting major touring exhibitions.

artEntertainment.name: Fort Point National Historic Site
artEntertainment.description: A stunning Civil War-era brick fortification beneath the Golden Gate Bridge, open for free ranger-led history talks and self-guided tours of its three floors of military history.

artEntertainment.name: Abbey Tavern
artEntertainment.type: Irish pub and live music venue
artEntertainment.description: A lively Inner Richmond Irish pub on Geary Boulevard hosting regular live music nights and the long-running Mirthquake Monday stand-up comedy show.

artEntertainment.name: 540 Club
artEntertainment.description: A popular Inner Richmond bar and live music showcase on Clement Street, known for an eclectic lineup of local and touring musical acts.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Visitor Center
artEntertainment.type: National park visitor center and exhibition space
artEntertainment.description: The gateway to the Presidio's history and natural resources, offering ranger programs, exhibits, Discovery Guides, and information for the park's 250th anniversary year.

gymsRecreation.name: Active Pilates
gymsRecreation.description: A small Clement Street studio offering small-group and private reformer Pilates and Gyrotonic classes for all levels.

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Golf Course
gymsRecreation.description: One of San Francisco's most scenic public golf courses, set within the Presidio's forested landscape with views of the bay, open to the public year-round.

gymsRecreation.name: Crissy Field
gymsRecreation.description: A restored tidal marsh and beach promenade along the Presidio's northern waterfront, popular for walking, running, windsurfing, kiteboarding, and picnicking with Golden Gate views.

gymsRecreation.name: Mountain Lake Park
gymsRecreation.description: A family- and dog-friendly park surrounding one of San Francisco's few remaining natural lakes, on the southern edge of the Presidio near Lake Street.

gymsRecreation.name: Land's End Trail
gymsRecreation.description: A scenic oceanfront trail along the northwestern tip of San Francisco offering dramatic views of the Golden Gate, Marin Headlands, and the ruins of Sutro Baths.
gymsRecreation.address: Point Lobos Ave & El Camino del Mar, Sea Cliff

gymsRecreation.name: Baker Beach
gymsRecreation.description: A stunning Presidio beach with sweeping views of the Golden Gate Bridge, popular for picnicking, fishing, and walking, with the northern end clothing-optional.

gymsRecreation.name: Richmond District YMCA
gymsRecreation.description: A full-service YMCA in the Inner Richmond offering fitness facilities, group exercise classes, youth programs, and community swimming.

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Running Co. / Sports Basement Presidio Trails
gymsRecreation.description: The Presidio's extensive network of wooded trails is a beloved destination for runners and walkers; Sports Basement Presidio hosts regular run club events on Saturdays.

gymsRecreation.name: Lincoln Park Golf Course
gymsRecreation.description: A scenic 18-hole public golf course in Lincoln Park with views of the Golden Gate Bridge, near the Legion of Honor museum.

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Pickleball Courts
gymsRecreation.description: Free public pickleball courts located within the Presidio park, available on a first-come basis and increasingly popular with Richmond and Presidio residents.
